items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: If I said Trane and Sonny, I wouldn’t even have to go further... The tenor was massively covered. Everybody had done something on it... I never sat and really copped Wayne... first I started out very Sonny. Sonny was in my head.

ctx.x: But even with Coltrane – I think Coltrane got his evenness from Dexter Gordon.

Dexter was more even. It’s true. And Pres was more even. And that’s the influence. That’s the Pres influence on Trane that no-one talks about. I think that’s a big influence on Trane, is the Pres influence, as compared to Hawk [Coleman Hawkins] with Sonny. You hear it. There’s a big difference. That boom boom boom-pa thing that Hawk was very – not heavy handed. He was emphatic. And Sonny taking that and, really, amazing what he did with it. And Trane coming, really, out of Pres, time-wise.

Actually, if you take it a step further back, Pres was very influenced by Bix Beiderbecke, who was basically – if you listen to Bix’s famous solo on Singin’ the Blues, from 1927, it’s an even eighth note solo.
